chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Azraq said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had a slave woman as a wife, then he married a free woman, and he did not inform the free woman that he had a slave woman. He said: 'If the free woman wishes, she may remain (in the marriage), and if she wishes, she may leave.' I said: 'She has already taken the dowry, so she will take it with her?' He said: 'Yes, for what he made permissible of her private part.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a free wife if her husband has a slave concubine and did not inform her?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the rights of a free wife when her husband secretly maintains a slave concubine, granting her the unilateral option (*khiyar*) to remain or depart. The Imam affirms that she retains her full dowry (*mahr*) as valid consideration for her consent to his sexual access, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the dowry is tied to the permissibility of intimacy rather than merely the contract's duration. This ruling underscores the importance of transparency in marital arrangements and the protection of the free wife’s financial and personal autonomy within the household structure.
